column1: # The worker guard's real-prompt regression corpus: command shapes dispatched
# planwright workers actually ran (or were prompted on), each with the verdict
# the guard must reach under every value of the `worker_self_approval` policy.
# tests/lib/worker-guard-corpus.sh documents the grammar, the sandbox the rows
# run in, and which suite replays which policy columns.
# <task> is the task whose landing ships the class; floor and uncovered name
# the task that began enforcing them.
# The four verdict columns are `allow` or `defer`, one per policy value: the
# empty list, `own-branch`, `scratch`, and both. A row of a `pending` class
# that stalls (expected allow, got defer) is reported but does not fail; once
# the task that delivers the class lands, it flips the class to `shipped` and
# every row of it is then enforced. A false-allow fails in every class.
# Floor and uncovered rows are enforced from the start and must defer under
# Sanitize every line to command shapes: no hostnames, user or machine
# paths, tokens, or repository names. A path is relative to the sandbox
# worktree, a fixed system location the shape needs (`/tmp`, `/dev/null`,
# `/`), or one of these placeholders, bound by the harness:
#   @@PLUGIN_ROOT@@  the installed planwright root under test
# Grow the corpus from live stalls: when a worker blocks on a command that
# should have been approved, add its sanitized shape here, under a shipped
# class, before fixing the guard, so the corpus fails until the fix lands and
